headline_marked: [[Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A 38-Billion-Parameter Model]] for Unified Embodied Synthesis
headline: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A 38-Billion-Parameter Model for Unified Embodied Synthesis
summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 is a 38-billion-parameter multimodal model designed for unified embodied synthesis, outperforming existing models in multi-view scene generation and embodied video tasks. It significantly improves robot manipulation success rates.
details: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 is a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive model for unified embodied synthesis. It directly extends foundation image and video generation to embodied scenarios, unlike traditional models that struggle with multi-view consistency and robot constraints.

This model jointly optimizes generative tasks like text-to-image generation, image editing, embodied scene generation, embodied transfer, and embodied video generation. It is the first to support high-quality multi-view scene generation across diverse robot embodiments with controllable transfer.

Its core innovation lies in a unified framework that integrates multiple generative tasks within a single optimization process. This contrasts with prior methods that often involve fine-tuning or adapting pre-trained models, potentially leading to a loss of general visual knowledge.

The model's architecture is designed to handle the unique requirements of embodied AI, ensuring multi-view consistency, geometric coherence, and incorporating robot embodiment constraints. This means generated content is realistic and compatible with various robot forms.

Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 has achieved state-of-the-art performance across various single-step and sequential generation tasks. In human evaluations for embodied scene generation and transfer, it outperformed GPT-Image-2.0 and ranked top on World Arena for embodied video generation.

For challenging real-world manipulation tasks, the model improved the out-of-distribution success rate of pi_0.5 from 36.9% to 63.2%. These results indicate that foundation world models can function effectively as both embodied world models and scalable data engines for embodied intelligence.

For developers in robotics and embodied AI, Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 offers a powerful new tool. Its ability to perform high-quality multi-view scene generation across multiple robot embodiments simplifies the creation of diverse and realistic simulation environments.

This can accelerate the development and testing of robot control policies and perception systems without the need for extensive real-world data collection. The structured, controllable embodied transfer provides fine-grained control over scene editing, crucial for iterating on robot task designs.

headline_marked: [[New Latent-Identity Tuning enables fine-grained facial edits]] in text-to-image models without retraining
headline: New Latent-Identity Tuning enables fine-grained facial edits in text-to-image models without retraining
summary: This innovative method modifies latent representations directly, allowing precise and consistent facial alterations across diverse image generations without the need for additional model training.
details: Latent-Identity Tuning offers highly precise facial edits in text-to-image models, overcoming limitations of traditional methods. It directly modifies the latent representation of an identity, ensuring consistency across generated images. This approach requires no additional training of the model.

The method explores the latent space of a pre-trained, frozen encoder to uncover semantic directions. These directions are linked to latent tokens, each capturing different aspects of an identity, often corresponding to specific facial regions.

By manipulating these latent tokens and their subspaces, the technique enables localized, fine-grained, and semantically coherent edits. This level of control was previously challenging with general-purpose models.

For instance, specific latent tokens might encode attributes like eyebrow shape or nose structure. Adjusting values along semantic directions associated with these tokens allows targeted modifications without affecting other features.

A key advantage is performing identity-level modifications without the computational cost and data requirements of additional model training. It leverages existing representations learned by the frozen encoder, making it efficient and scalable.

Developers can integrate Latent-Identity Tuning to create more sophisticated identity personalization tools. This allows for subtle alterations like expressions, eye color, or aging effects while maintaining consistent identity.
The absence of extra training simplifies deployment, as developers can use existing pre-trained models. This lowers the barrier to entry for precise facial editing in generative AI applications.
